metadata.title: Introduction to the non-asymptotic analysis of random matrices
metadata.venue: Chapter 5 of Compressed Sensing, Theory and Applications (Eldar & Kutyniok eds.), Cambridge UP

nodes.name: Singular values of a matrix
nodes.statement: The eigenvalues of $|A| := \sqrt{A^*A}$, arranged in non-increasing order $s_1(A) \ge \cdots \ge s_n(A) \ge 0$, are the singular values of $A$; $\smax(A) := s_1(A)$, $\smin(A) := s_n(A)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Singular values are the non-negative eigenvalues of $\sqrt{A^*A}$.

nodes.name: Spectral norm
nodes.statement: $\|A\| = \sup_{x \in \R^n \setminus \{0\}} \frac{\|Ax\|_2}{\|x\|_2} = \sup_{x \in S^{n-1}} \|Ax\|_2$; equals $\smax(A)$.

nodes.name: Nets, covering numbers
nodes.statement: An $\e$-net of metric space $(X,d)$ is a subset $\NN_\e \subseteq X$ with $d(x,\NN_\e) \le \e$ for all $x \in X$. The covering number $\NN(X,\e)$ is its minimal cardinality.

nodes.name: Covering numbers of the sphere
nodes.statement: The unit sphere $S^{n-1}$ satisfies $\NN(S^{n-1},\e) \le \big( 1 + \frac{2}{\e} \big)^n$ for every $\e > 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.1 (volume argument)
nodes.statement: Volume argument: a maximal $\e$-separated set $\NN_\e$ on $S^{n-1}$ is itself an $\e$-net; its $\e/2$-balls are disjoint inside $(1+\e/2)B_2^n$, giving $|\NN_\e| \le (1+2/\e)^n$.

nodes.name: Construct maximal $\e$-separated set
nodes.statement: Fix $\e>0$ and choose $\NN_\e \subseteq S^{n-1}$ to be a maximal $\e$-separated subset, i.e. $d(x,y)\ge\e$ for distinct $x,y\in\NN_\e$.

nodes.name: Maximality implies net property
nodes.statement: Maximality forces $\NN_\e$ to be an $\e$-net of $S^{n-1}$: otherwise some $x\in S^{n-1}$ would be $\e$-far from all points, and $\NN_\e\cup\{x\}$ would still be $\e$-separated.

nodes.name: Disjoint balls + volume comparison
nodes.statement: By separation, balls $B(x_i,\e/2)$ for $x_i\in\NN_\e$ are disjoint and lie in $(1+\e/2)B_2^n$. Volume comparison: $|\NN_\e| \le (1+\e/2)^n / (\e/2)^n = (1+2/\e)^n$.

nodes.name: Computing the spectral norm on a net
nodes.statement: For an $N\times n$ matrix $A$ and $\e$-net $\NN_\e$ of $S^{n-1}$ ($\e\in[0,1)$): $\max_{x \in \NN_\e} \|Ax\|_2 \le \|A\| \le (1-\e)^{-1} \max_{x \in \NN_\e} \|Ax\|_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.2
nodes.statement: Lower bound trivial; for upper bound, take $x\in S^{n-1}$ attaining $\|A\|$ and $y\in\NN_\e$ with $\|x-y\|\le\e$; triangle inequality gives $\|Ay\|_2 \ge (1-\e)\|A\|$.

nodes.name: Spectral norm on a net (symmetric case)
nodes.statement: For a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix $A$ and an $\e$-net $\NN_\e$ of $S^{n-1}$ with $\e\in[0,1)$: $\|A\| \le (1-2\e)^{-1} \sup_{x\in\NN_\e} |\langle Ax,x\rangle|$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.3
nodes.statement: Pick $x\in S^{n-1}$ with $\|A\|=|\langle Ax,x\rangle|$ and $y\in\NN_\e$ within $\e$; triangle inequality gives $|\langle Ax,x\rangle - \langle Ay,y\rangle| \le 2\e\|A\|$.

nodes.name: Equivalence of sub-gaussian properties
nodes.statement: Tail $\P\{|X|>t\} \le \exp(1-t^2/K_1^2)$, moment $(\E|X|^p)^{1/p}\le K_2\sqrt p$, super-exp moment $\E\exp(X^2/K_3^2)\le e$ are equivalent up to absolute constants; if $\E X=0$ also mgf $\E\exp(tX)\le\exp(t^2 K_4^2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.4 (cyclic implications)
nodes.statement: Cyclic implications $1\Rightarrow 2 \Rightarrow 3 \Rightarrow 1$ via integration by parts, Taylor expansion of $\exp(cX^2)$, exponential Markov; plus $2\Rightarrow 4$ and $4\Rightarrow 1$ for the centered case.

nodes.name: $1\Rightarrow 2$: tail to moments
nodes.statement: Use $\E|X|^p = \int_0^\infty \P\{|X|\ge t\} p t^{p-1} dt \le \int_0^\infty e^{1-t^2} p t^{p-1} dt$; integral evaluates to $\le (ep/2)^{p/2+1}$, taking $p$-th root gives moment bound.

nodes.name: $2\Rightarrow 3$: moments to $\psi_2$ integrability
nodes.statement: Taylor expand $\E\exp(cX^2) = 1 + \sum c^p \E X^{2p}/p! \le 1 + \sum (2c/e)^p$, finite for small $c$; then $K_3 = c^{-1/2}$.

nodes.name: $3\Rightarrow 1$: integrability to tail
nodes.statement: Exponential Markov: $\P\{|X|>t\} = \P\{e^{X^2} \ge e^{t^2}\} \le e^{-t^2}\E e^{X^2} \le e^{1-t^2}$.

nodes.name: $2\Rightarrow 4$: moments to mgf (centered case)
nodes.statement: Compare Taylor series $\E\exp(tX) \le 1+\sum (e|t|/\sqrt p)^p$ with $\exp(C^2 t^2) = 1+\sum(C|t|/\sqrt{p/2})^p$; second dominates first for large $C$.

nodes.name: $4\Rightarrow 1$: mgf to tail
nodes.statement: Exponential Markov on $e^{\lambda X}$: $\P\{X\ge t\} \le e^{-\lambda t + \lambda^2}$; optimize $\lambda=t/2$ to get $e^{-t^2/4}$.

nodes.name: Sub-gaussian random variable; sub-gaussian norm
nodes.statement: $X$ is sub-gaussian if it satisfies any equivalent property of Lemma~LP9.4; $\|X\|_{\psi_2} = \sup_{p\ge 1} p^{-1/2}(\E|X|^p)^{1/p}$.

nodes.name: Sub-gaussian random variables: Gaussian, Bernoulli, bounded
nodes.statement: Standard Gaussian $X$ has $\|X\|_{\psi_2}\le C$. Symmetric Bernoulli has $\|X\|_{\psi_2}=1$. Any bounded $X$ has $\|X\|_{\psi_2}\le \|X\|_\infty$.

nodes.name: Rotation invariance
nodes.statement: For independent centered sub-gaussian $X_i$, $\sum_i X_i$ is centered sub-gaussian with $\big\|\sum_i X_i\big\|_{\psi_2}^2 \le C\sum_i \|X_i\|_{\psi_2}^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.5 (mgf product)
nodes.statement: Independence and mgf bound (property 4 of LP9.4) give $\E\exp(t\sum X_i) = \prod \E\exp(tX_i) \le \exp(t^2 K^2)$ with $K^2 = C\sum\|X_i\|_{\psi_2}^2$; then property $2\Leftrightarrow 4$ gives $\psi_2$ bound.

nodes.name: Hoeffding-type inequality (sub-gaussian large deviations)
nodes.statement: For independent centered sub-gaussian $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ with $K=\max_i\|X_i\|_{\psi_2}$ and $a\in\R^N$: $\P\big\{|\sum a_i X_i| \ge t\big\} \le e\exp(-ct^2/(K^2\|a\|_2^2))$.

nodes.name: Proof of PrP9.1
nodes.statement: Rotation invariance (LP9.5) gives $\|\sum a_i X_i\|_{\psi_2}^2 \le CK^2\|a\|_2^2$; sub-gaussian tail bound (LP9.4 property 1) yields the result.

nodes.name: Khintchine inequality
nodes.statement: For independent sub-gaussian $X_i$ with mean 0, variance 1, $\|X_i\|_{\psi_2}\le K$, and any $p\ge 2$, $a_i$: $(\sum a_i^2)^{1/2} \le (\E|\sum a_i X_i|^p)^{1/p} \le CK\sqrt p (\sum a_i^2)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.1
nodes.statement: Lower bound by H\"older's inequality. Upper bound by rotation invariance applied with the moment-growth property (LP9.4 property 2).

nodes.name: Sub-exponential random variable; $\psi_1$ norm
nodes.statement: $X$ is sub-exponential if it satisfies any of: tail $\P\{|X|>t\}\le\exp(1-t/K_1)$, moments $(\E|X|^p)^{1/p}\le K_2 p$, $\E\exp(X/K_3)\le e$. Norm $\|X\|_{\psi_1} = \sup_{p\ge 1} p^{-1}(\E|X|^p)^{1/p}$.

nodes.name: Sub-exponential is sub-gaussian squared
nodes.statement: $X$ is sub-gaussian iff $X^2$ is sub-exponential; $\|X\|_{\psi_2}^2 \le \|X^2\|_{\psi_1} \le 2\|X\|_{\psi_2}^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.6
nodes.statement: Direct from definitions: moment growth $(\E|X^2|^p)^{1/p} = (\E|X|^{2p})^{1/p}$ relates the two norms.

nodes.name: Mgf of sub-exponential random variables
nodes.statement: For centered sub-exponential $X$ and $|t|\le c/\|X\|_{\psi_1}$: $\E\exp(tX) \le \exp(Ct^2 \|X\|_{\psi_1}^2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.7
nodes.statement: Repeat $2\Rightarrow 4$ argument of LP9.4 with $\E|X|^p \le p^p$: $\E\exp(tX) \le 1+\sum(e|t|)^p \le \exp(2e^2 t^2)$ for $|t|\le 1/(2e)$.

nodes.name: Bernstein-type inequality (sub-exponential large deviations)
nodes.statement: For independent centered sub-exponential $X_i$, $K=\max_i\|X_i\|_{\psi_1}$, $a\in\R^N$: $\P\big\{|\sum a_i X_i|\ge t\big\} \le 2\exp[-c\min(t^2/(K^2\|a\|_2^2),\, t/(K\|a\|_\infty))]$.

nodes.name: Proof of PrP9.2
nodes.statement: Exponential Markov on $S=\sum a_i X_i$ with parameter $\lambda$, mgf bound from LP9.7 (valid for $|\lambda|\le c/\|a\|_\infty$), then optimize $\lambda = \min(t/(2C\|a\|_2^2),\, c/\|a\|_\infty)$.

nodes.name: Apply exponential Markov
nodes.statement: $\P\{S\ge t\} = \P\{e^{\lambda S}\ge e^{\lambda t}\} \le e^{-\lambda t}\prod_i \E\exp(\lambda a_i X_i)$.

nodes.name: Bound mgf by LP9.7
nodes.statement: If $|\lambda| \le c/\|a\|_\infty$ then $|\lambda a_i| \le c$, so by LP9.7 each factor $\le \exp(C\lambda^2 a_i^2)$; product gives $\exp(-\lambda t + C\lambda^2 \|a\|_2^2)$.

nodes.name: Optimize $\lambda$ and combine tails
nodes.statement: Choose $\lambda = \min(t/(2C\|a\|_2^2), c/\|a\|_\infty)$; the two cases give the gaussian/exponential mixed tail. Repeat for $-X_i$ to bound both tails.

nodes.name: Average sub-exponentials concentration
nodes.statement: For independent centered sub-exponential $X_i$ with $K=\max\|X_i\|_{\psi_1}$ and any $\e\ge 0$: $\P\{|\sum_{i=1}^N X_i|\ge\e N\} \le 2\exp[-c\min(\e^2/K^2,\,\e/K)N]$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.2
nodes.statement: Apply PrP9.2 with $a_i=1$ and $t=\e N$.

nodes.name: Isotropic random vector
nodes.statement: A random vector $X$ in $\R^n$ is isotropic if $\Sigma(X) = \E X\otimes X = I$, equivalently $\E\langle X,x\rangle^2 = \|x\|_2^2$ for all $x \in \R^n$.

nodes.name: Norm and inner product of isotropic vectors
nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are independent isotropic in $\R^n$, then $\E\|X\|_2^2 = n$ and $\E\langle X,Y\rangle^2 = n$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.8
nodes.statement: $\E\|X\|_2^2 = \E\tr(X\otimes X) = \tr(I) = n$. For $\langle X,Y\rangle^2$, condition on $Y$ and use isotropy of $X$.

nodes.name: Examples of isotropic random vectors
nodes.statement: Gaussian $N(0,I)$, Bernoulli (i.i.d. $\pm 1$ coordinates), product distributions with mean 0 variance 1, coordinate vector uniform on $\{\sqrt n\, e_i\}$, tight frames with $A=B=M$, spherical of radius $\sqrt n$, uniform on isotropic convex sets.

nodes.name: Sub-gaussian random vector
nodes.statement: $X$ in $\R^n$ is sub-gaussian if all 1-D marginals $\langle X,x\rangle$ are sub-gaussian; $\|X\|_{\psi_2} = \sup_{x\in S^{n-1}} \|\langle X,x\rangle\|_{\psi_2}$.

nodes.name: Product of sub-gaussian distributions
nodes.statement: For independent centered sub-gaussian $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, the vector $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ is centered sub-gaussian with $\|X\|_{\psi_2} \le C\max_{i\le n}\|X_i\|_{\psi_2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.9
nodes.statement: For $x\in S^{n-1}$, by rotation invariance LP9.5: $\|\langle X,x\rangle\|_{\psi_2}^2 \le C\sum x_i^2 \|X_i\|_{\psi_2}^2 \le C\max\|X_i\|_{\psi_2}^2$.

nodes.name: Non-commutative Khintchine inequality
nodes.statement: For self-adjoint $n\times n$ matrices $A_i$ and independent symmetric Bernoulli $\e_i$, $2\le p<\infty$: $\big\|(\sum A_i^2)^{1/2}\big\|_{C_p^n} \le (\E\|\sum\e_i A_i\|_{C_p^n}^p)^{1/p} \le C\sqrt p\,\big\|(\sum A_i^2)^{1/2}\big\|_{C_p^n}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Lust-Piquard; Pisier, Operator Space Theory, Section 9.8

nodes.name: Rudelson's inequality
nodes.statement: For vectors $x_i\in\R^n$ and independent symmetric Bernoulli $\e_i$: $\E\big\|\sum_{i=1}^N \e_i x_i\otimes x_i\big\| \le C\sqrt{\log\min(N,n)}\cdot\max_i\|x_i\|_2 \cdot \big\|\sum_i x_i\otimes x_i\big\|^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.3
nodes.statement: Reduce to $n\le N$ by restriction to span; then apply spectral-norm version of TP9.1 with $A_i = x_i\otimes x_i$, using $(x_i\otimes x_i)^2 = \|x_i\|_2^2 \, x_i\otimes x_i$.

nodes.name: Non-commutative Bernstein-type inequality (matrix Bernstein)
nodes.statement: For independent centered self-adjoint $n\times n$ random matrices $X_i$ with $\|X_i\|\le K$ a.s.\ and $\|\sum_i\E X_i^2\|\le\sigma^2$: $\P\{\|\sum X_i\|\ge t\} \le 2n\exp(-t^2/2 / (\sigma^2 + Kt/3))$.

nodes.name: Bai-Yin's law
nodes.statement: For $N\times n$ random matrix $A$ with i.i.d.\ entries (mean 0, variance 1, finite 4th moment), as $N,n\to\infty$ with $n/N\to$ const $\in[0,1]$: $\smin(A) = \sqrt N - \sqrt n + o(\sqrt n)$, $\smax(A) = \sqrt N + \sqrt n + o(\sqrt n)$ a.s.

nodes.name: Gordon's theorem for Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement: For $N\times n$ matrix $A$ with i.i.d.\ standard normal entries: $\sqrt N - \sqrt n \le \E\smin(A) \le \E\smax(A) \le \sqrt N + \sqrt n$.

nodes.name: Slepian's inequality
nodes.statement: For Gaussian processes $(X_t),(Y_t)$ on $T$ with $\E|X_s-X_t|^2 \le \E|Y_s-Y_t|^2$: $\E\sup_t X_t \le \E\sup_t Y_t$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.4 (Gordon via Slepian)
nodes.statement: Express $\smax(A)$ as supremum of Gaussian process $X_{u,v}=\langle Au,v\rangle$ on $S^{n-1}\times S^{N-1}$, dominate by simpler $Y_{u,v}=\langle g,u\rangle+\langle h,v\rangle$, apply Slepian to get $\E\smax(A)\le \E\|g\|+\E\|h\| \le \sqrt n + \sqrt N$. Lower bound via Gordon's minimax extension.

nodes.name: Identify $\smax$ as supremum of Gaussian process
nodes.statement: $\smax(A) = \max_{u,v} \langle Au,v\rangle$ over $S^{n-1}\times S^{N-1}$. Set $X_{u,v} = \langle Au,v\rangle$, $Y_{u,v}=\langle g,u\rangle+\langle h,v\rangle$ with independent $g\in\R^n$, $h\in\R^N$ standard normal.

nodes.name: Apply Slepian and bound RHS
nodes.statement: By Slepian (LP9.10), $\E\sup X \le \E\sup Y = \E\|g\|_2 + \E\|h\|_2 \le \sqrt n + \sqrt N$.

nodes.name: Lower bound via Gordon
nodes.statement: Bound $\E\smin(A) = \E\max_v\min_u\langle Au,v\rangle$ via Gordon's minimax extension of Slepian.

nodes.name: Concentration in Gauss space
nodes.statement: For $K$-Lipschitz $f:\R^n\to\R$ and standard normal $X$: $\P\{f(X)-\E f(X) > t\} \le \exp(-t^2/(2K^2))$.

nodes.name: Gaussian matrices, deviation
nodes.statement: For $N\times n$ matrix $A$ with i.i.d.\ standard normal entries and $t\ge 0$, with prob $\ge 1-2\exp(-t^2/2)$: $\sqrt N -\sqrt n - t \le \smin(A) \le \smax(A) \le \sqrt N + \sqrt n + t$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.4
nodes.statement: $\smin,\smax$ are 1-Lipschitz functions of $A\in\R^{Nn}$; combine TP9.4 (expectation bound) with Gaussian concentration PrP9.3.

nodes.name: Approximate isometries
nodes.statement: If $\|B^*B-I\| \le \max(\delta,\delta^2)$ then $1-\delta \le \smin(B) \le \smax(B) \le 1+\delta$. Conversely, $1-\delta\le\smin\le\smax\le 1+\delta$ implies $\|B^*B-I\|\le 3\max(\delta,\delta^2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.11
nodes.statement: Both inequalities reduce to estimates on $|\|Bx\|_2 - 1|$ for $x \in S^{n-1}$ via the elementary inequality $\max(|z-1|,|z-1|^2) \le |z^2-1| \le 3\max(|z-1|,|z-1|^2)$ for $z \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Latala's theorem
nodes.statement: For random matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ with independent centered entries (finite 4th moment): $\E\smax(A) \le C[\max_i(\sum_j\E a_{ij}^2)^{1/2} + \max_j(\sum_i\E a_{ij}^2)^{1/2} + (\sum_{i,j}\E a_{ij}^4)^{1/4}]$.

nodes.name: Hard edge for square matrices with independent entries
nodes.statement: For $n\times n$ matrix $A$ with i.i.d.\ subgaussian entries (mean 0, variance 1), $\e\ge 0$: $\P(\smin(A) \le \e(\sqrt N - \sqrt{n-1})) \le (C\e)^{N-n+1} + c^N$.

nodes.name: Sub-gaussian rows
nodes.statement: For $A$ ($N\times n$) with independent sub-gaussian isotropic rows in $\R^n$ and $t\ge 0$, with prob $\ge 1-2\exp(-ct^2)$: $\sqrt N - C\sqrt n - t \le \smin(A) \le \smax(A) \le \sqrt N + C\sqrt n + t$. Constants $C=C_K, c=c_K$ depend on $K=\max\|A_i\|_{\psi_2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.7 (covering argument)
nodes.statement: Three-step covering argument: (1) reduce to controlling $\|N^{-1}A^*A - I\|$ on a $1/4$-net of $S^{n-1}$; (2) for each fixed $x$, $\|Ax\|_2^2$ is sum of independent sub-exp $Z_i^2$ controlled by CP9.2; (3) union bound over net of size $9^n$.

nodes.name: Approximation step (net reduction)
nodes.statement: By LP9.11, conclusion $\Leftrightarrow \|N^{-1}A^*A-I\|\le\max(\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=C\sqrt{n/N}+t/\sqrt N$. By LP9.3 with a $1/4$-net $\NN$ of $S^{n-1}$ (cardinality $\le 9^n$ via LP9.1), reduce to $\max_{x\in\NN}|N^{-1}\|Ax\|^2 - 1| \le \e/2$.

nodes.name: Concentration for fixed $x$
nodes.statement: Fix $x\in S^{n-1}$: $\|Ax\|_2^2 = \sum Z_i^2$ with $Z_i = \langle A_i, x\rangle$ independent sub-gaussian, $\E Z_i^2 = 1$. Then $Z_i^2-1$ are sub-exponential with $\|\cdot\|_{\psi_1}\le 4K^2$. Apply CP9.2 to bound $\P\{|N^{-1}\sum Z_i^2 - 1| \ge \e/2\} \le 2\exp(-c_1(C^2 n + t^2)/K^4)$.

nodes.name: Union bound over net
nodes.statement: Multiply tail bound by $|\NN|\le 9^n$ and choose $C=K^2\sqrt{\ln 9/c_1}$ to absorb the $9^n$ factor: $\P\{\max_{x\in\NN}|N^{-1}\|Ax\|^2-1|\ge\e/2\} \le 2\exp(-c_1 t^2/K^4)$.

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed rows
nodes.statement: For $A$ with independent isotropic rows in $\R^n$ and $\|A_i\|_2 \le \sqrt m$ a.s.: with prob $\ge 1-2n\exp(-ct^2)$, $\sqrt N - t\sqrt m \le \smin(A) \le \smax(A) \le \sqrt N + t\sqrt m$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.8 (matrix Bernstein)
nodes.statement: Three steps: (1) reduce to $\|N^{-1}\sum X_i\|\le\e$ where $X_i = N^{-1}(A_i\otimes A_i - I)$; (2) estimate range $\|X_i\|\le 2m/N$ and total variance $\|\sum\E X_i^2\| \le 2m/N$; (3) apply matrix Bernstein TP9.2.

nodes.name: Reduce to sum of independent matrices
nodes.statement: By LP9.11, target $\|N^{-1}A^*A-I\|\le\max(\delta,\delta^2)=:\e$, $\delta=t\sqrt{m/N}$. Write $N^{-1}A^*A-I = \sum X_i$ where $X_i=N^{-1}(A_i\otimes A_i - I)$ are independent centered matrices.

nodes.name: Estimate range and variance
nodes.statement: Range: $\|X_i\| \le N^{-1}(\|A_i\|_2^2 + 1) \le 2m/N =: K$. Variance: $\E X_i^2 = N^{-2}[\E(A_i\otimes A_i)^2 - I]$ with $\|\E(A_i\otimes A_i)^2\| \le m$, giving $\|\sum\E X_i^2\|\le 2m/N =:\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Apply matrix Bernstein
nodes.statement: Apply TP9.2 (with mixed-tail Remark): $\P\{\|\sum X_i\|\ge\e\} \le 2n\exp[-c\min(\e^2/\sigma^2,\e/K)] = 2n\exp(-ct^2/2)$.

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed rows, non-isotropic
nodes.statement: For $A$ with independent rows having common $\Sigma=\E A_i\otimes A_i$ and $\|A_i\|_2\le\sqrt m$ a.s., $t\ge 0$, with prob $\ge 1-n\exp(-ct^2)$: $\|N^{-1}A^*A-\Sigma\| \le \max(\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=t\sqrt{m/N}$. Also $\|A\|\le\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt N + t\sqrt m$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.9
nodes.statement: First inequality by straightforward modification of the proof of TP9.8 noting $m\ge\|\Sigma\|$. Second follows by triangle inequality on $\|N^{-1}A^*A\|$ and taking square roots.

nodes.name: Symmetrization
nodes.statement: For independent random vectors $X_i$ in a Banach space and independent symmetric Bernoulli $\e_i$: $\E\|\sum(X_i-\E X_i)\| \le 2\E\|\sum\e_i X_i\|$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.12
nodes.statement: Introduce independent copy $X_i'$, set $\tilde X_i = X_i-X_i'$. Sequence $(\tilde X_i)$ has same law as $(\e_i\tilde X_i)$. Jensen + triangle: $\E\|\sum(X_i-\E X_i)\| \le \E\|\sum\tilde X_i\| = \E\|\sum\e_i\tilde X_i\| \le 2\E\|\sum\e_i X_i\|$.

nodes.name: Probabilistic deviation from 1
nodes.statement: For non-negative random variable $Z$: $\E|Z^2-1| \ge \max(\E|Z-1|, (\E|Z-1|)^2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.13
nodes.statement: Pointwise $|Z-1|\le|Z^2-1|$ gives the linear bound; pointwise $|Z-1|^2\le|Z^2-1|$ plus Jensen gives the quadratic bound.

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed rows; expected singular values
nodes.statement: For $A$ with independent isotropic rows and $m=\E\max_{i\le N}\|A_i\|_2^2$: $\E\max_{j\le n}|s_j(A)-\sqrt N| \le C\sqrt{m\log\min(N,n)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.10 (Rudelson + diagonalization)
nodes.statement: Two-step: (1) bound $E:=\E\|N^{-1}A^*A-I\|$ by symmetrization LP9.12 then Rudelson CP9.3, getting Cauchy-Schwarz inequality $E\le C\sqrt{ml/N}(E+1)^{1/2}$ which solves to $E\le\max(\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=C\sqrt{2ml/N}$; (2) diagonalize $A^*A$ and apply LP9.13 separately to $\smin,\smax$.

nodes.name: Symmetrization + Rudelson application
nodes.statement: $E = \E\|N^{-1}\sum A_i\otimes A_i - I\| \le (2/N)\E\|\sum\e_i A_i\otimes A_i\|$ by LP9.12. Conditional on $A$, apply CP9.3 then take expectation: $E \le (C\sqrt l/N)\E(\max_i\|A_i\|_2 \cdot \|\sum A_i\otimes A_i\|^{1/2})$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and solve quadratic
nodes.statement: Cauchy-Schwarz with $\E\|N^{-1}\sum A_i\otimes A_i\| \le E+1$ gives $E \le C\sqrt{ml/N}(E+1)^{1/2}$. Solving in cases $E\le 1, E>1$: $E\le\max(\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=C\sqrt{2ml/N}$.

nodes.name: Diagonalization step
nodes.statement: $\|N^{-1}A^*A - I\| = \max_j|s_j(A)^2/N - 1|$. Apply LP9.13 separately to $\smin/\sqrt N, \smax/\sqrt N$ to convert quadratic deviation to linear; sum the two terms gives the bound.

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed rows, non-isotropic, expectation
nodes.statement: For $A$ with independent rows having common $\Sigma=\E A_i\otimes A_i$ and $m=\E\max\|A_i\|_2^2$: $\E\|N^{-1}A^*A-\Sigma\| \le \max(\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=C\sqrt{m\log\min(N,n)/N}$. Hence $(\E\|A\|^2)^{1/2} \le \|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\sqrt N + C\sqrt{m\log\min(N,n)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.11
nodes.statement: Modification of TP9.10 proof for non-isotropic case; second part follows from first by triangle inequality argument as in TP9.9.

nodes.name: Covariance estimation for sub-gaussian distributions
nodes.statement: For sub-gaussian distribution in $\R^n$ with covariance $\Sigma$, $\e\in(0,1), t\ge 1$: with prob $\ge 1-2\exp(-t^2 n)$, if $N\ge C(t/\e)^2 n$ then $\|\Sigma_N - \Sigma\| \le \e$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.5
nodes.statement: Apply non-isotropic version of TP9.7 (Remark r:non-isotropic) with $s = C't\sqrt n$ for sufficiently large $C'_K$.

nodes.name: Covariance estimation for arbitrary (heavy-tailed) distributions
nodes.statement: For distribution in $\R^n$ with covariance $\Sigma$ supported in centered Euclidean ball of radius $\sqrt m$, $\e\in(0,1), t\ge 1$: with prob $\ge 1-n^{-t^2}$, if $N\ge C(t/\e)^2 \|\Sigma\|^{-1} m\log n$ then $\|\Sigma_N - \Sigma\| \le \e\|\Sigma\|$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.6
nodes.statement: From TP9.9: with prob $\ge 1-n\exp(-cs^2)$, $\|\Sigma_N-\Sigma\|\le\max(\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=s\sqrt{m/N}$. Choose $s=C't\sqrt{\log n}$.

nodes.name: Random sub-matrices
nodes.statement: For $M\times n$ matrix $B$ with $\smin(B)=\smax(B)=\sqrt M$ and $\|B_i\|_2\le\sqrt m$, sampling $N$ rows uniformly i.i.d.\ to form $A$: with prob $\ge 1-2n\exp(-ct^2)$, $\sqrt N - t\sqrt m \le \smin(A) \le \smax(A) \le \sqrt N + t\sqrt m$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.7
nodes.statement: Hypothesis $I = M^{-1}B^*B = M^{-1}\sum B_i\otimes B_i$ implies uniform distribution on $\{B_i\}$ is isotropic; apply TP9.8.

nodes.name: Random sub-frames
nodes.statement: For tight frame $\{u_i\}_{i=1}^M$ in $\R^n$ with $A=B=M$ and $\|u_i\|_2\le\sqrt m$, sampling $N$ uniformly: with prob $\ge 1-2n^{-t^2}$, if $N\ge C(t/\e)^2 m\log n$ then $\{v_i\}_{i=1}^N$ is a frame with bounds $A=(1-\e)N, B=(1+\e)N$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP9.8
nodes.statement: Frame condition gives $I = M^{-1}\sum u_i\otimes u_i$, so uniform distribution on $\{u_i\}$ is isotropic. Apply CP9.6 with $\Sigma=I$.

nodes.name: Decoupling (double array)
nodes.statement: For double array $(a_{ij})$ with $a_{ii}=0$: $\sum_{i,j\in[n]} a_{ij} = 4\E\sum_{i\in T,j\in T^c} a_{ij}$ where $T$ is a random subset of $[n]$ with average size $n/2$. In particular $\sum a_{ij}$ is between $4\min_T$ and $4\max_T$ of the partial sum.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.14
nodes.statement: Express $T$ via independent selectors $\delta_i$ with $\E\delta_i=1/2$; $\E\delta_i(1-\delta_j)=1/4$ for $i\ne j$, and $a_{ii}=0$ disposes of the diagonal.

nodes.name: Sub-gaussian columns
nodes.statement: For $A$ ($N\ge n$) with independent sub-gaussian isotropic columns $A_j\in\R^N$, $\|A_j\|_2=\sqrt N$ a.s., $t\ge 0$: with prob $\ge 1-2\exp(-ct^2)$, $\sqrt N - C\sqrt n - t \le \smin(A) \le \smax(A) \le \sqrt N + C\sqrt n + t$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.12 (decoupling + covering)
nodes.statement: Four steps: (1) reductions: zero-mean WLOG, control $\|A\|$ by transposition + TP9.7; (2) $1/4$-net approximation; (3) decoupling via LP9.14 to express off-diagonal Gram form via random subset $T$; (4) condition on $A_{T^c}$ to get sum of independent sub-gaussian terms, apply tail bound, union bound.

nodes.name: Reductions and a priori bound on $\|A\|$
nodes.statement: WLOG $A_i$ centered (multiply by $\pm 1$). For $t\ge C_K\sqrt N$ result follows from transposition + TP9.7. So assume $t\le C_K\sqrt N$ and define event $\EE = \{\smax(A)\le 3C_K\sqrt N\}$ with $\P(\EE^c)\le 2\exp(-c_K t^2)$.

nodes.name: Approximation on $1/4$-net
nodes.statement: Let $\NN$ be a $1/4$-net of $S^{n-1}$, $|\NN|\le 9^n$. Reduce to showing $\P\{\max_{x\in\NN}|N^{-1}\|Ax\|^2 - 1| > \delta/2 \text{ and }\EE\} \le 2\exp(-c_K'' t^2)$.

nodes.name: Decoupling
nodes.statement: Expand $\|Ax\|_2^2 = \sum x_j^2 \|A_j\|^2 + \sum_{j\ne k} x_j x_k\langle A_j, A_k\rangle = N + \langle G_0 x, x\rangle$. Apply LP9.14 to $G_0$ to get $|N^{-1}\|Ax\|^2 - 1| \le (4/N)\max_T |R_T(x)|$, $R_T(x)=\sum_{j\in T,k\in T^c} x_j x_k\langle A_j,A_k\rangle$. Union bound over $\NN$ and $2^n$ subsets.

nodes.name: Conditioning + sub-gaussian concentration
nodes.statement: Condition on $(A_k)_{k\in T^c}$: $R_T(x) = \sum_{j\in T} x_j\langle A_j, z\rangle$ with $z=\sum_{k\in T^c}x_k A_k$ fixed, $\|z\|\le 3C_K\sqrt N$ on $\EE$. Each $\langle A_j,z\rangle$ is sub-gaussian; rotation invariance LP9.5 gives $\|R_T(x)\|_{\psi_2}\le \widehat C_K\sqrt N$. Sub-gaussian tail and union bound complete the proof.

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed columns
nodes.statement: For $A$ ($N\ge n$) with independent isotropic columns $A_j\in\R^N$, $\|A_j\|_2=\sqrt N$ a.s., and incoherence $m = N^{-1}\E\max_j\sum_{k\ne j}\langle A_j,A_k\rangle^2$: $\E\|N^{-1}A^*A-I\| \le C_0\sqrt{m\log n/N}$, hence $\E\max_j |s_j(A)-\sqrt N| \le C\sqrt{m\log n}$.

nodes.name: Matrix decoupling
nodes.statement: For $N\times n$ random matrix $B$ with $\|B_j\|_2=1$: $\E\|B^*B-I\| \le 4\max_{T\subseteq[n]} \E\|(B_T)^* B_{T^c}\|$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.15
nodes.statement: Expand $\|Bx\|^2 - 1$ for $x\in S^{n-1}$, apply LP9.14 to off-diagonal sum to get random-subset form, then Jensen + sup-max.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.13
nodes.statement: Three steps: (1) a priori bound $\E\|A\|\le C\sqrt{N\log n}$ via transposition + TP9.10; matrix decoupling LP9.15 reduces to $\E\|\Gamma\|$ for decoupled Gram block $\Gamma=(A_T)^* A_{T^c}$; (2) conditional on $A_{T^c}$, $\Gamma$ has independent rows; estimate row-norms and second-moment matrices; (3) apply TP9.11 to bound $\E\|\Gamma\|$, take expectation in $A_{T^c}$.

nodes.name: Reductions: norm bound + matrix decoupling
nodes.statement: Apply TP9.10 to $A^*$: $\E\|A\|\le C\sqrt{N\log n}$. Note $n\le m$. By LP9.15: $E \le (4/N)\max_T \E\|\Gamma\|$ where $\Gamma=(A_T)^* A_{T^c}$ is the decoupled Gram matrix.

nodes.name: Conditional analysis of rows of $\Gamma$
nodes.statement: Conditioning on $A_{T^c}$, $\Gamma$ has independent rows $\Gamma_j=(\langle A_j,A_k\rangle)_{k\in T^c}$. (a) Second-moment matrix: by isotropy, $\|\Sigma(\Gamma_j)\| \le \|A_{T^c}\|^2$. (b) Row-norm: $\E_{A_T}\max_j\|\Gamma_j\|^2 \le N\E_{A_T}M$ where $M$ is the conditional incoherence variable.

nodes.name: Bound $\E\|\Gamma\|$ via TP9.11 and combine
nodes.statement: By TP9.11 (with non-identical $\Sigma_i$ remark): $\E_{A_T}\|\Gamma\| \le \|A_{T^c}\|\sqrt n + C\sqrt{N\E_{A_T}(M)\log n}$. Take expectation in $A_{T^c}$: $\E\|A_{T^c}\| \le C\sqrt{N\log n}$, $\E\sqrt{\E_{A_T} M} \le \sqrt m$. Combine with $n\le m$: $\E\|\Gamma\|\le 2C\sqrt{Nm\log n}$, hence $E\le 8C\sqrt{m\log n/N}$.

nodes.name: Diagonalization (singular-value form)
nodes.statement: Apply diagonalization argument as in PSP9.24 (Step 2 of TP9.10 proof) to convert $\E\|N^{-1}A^*A-I\|$ into bound on $\E\max_j|s_j(A)-\sqrt N|$.

nodes.name: Restricted isometry property; restricted isometry constant
nodes.statement: An $m\times n$ matrix $A$ has the restricted isometry property of order $k$ if there exists $\delta_k\ge 0$ such that $(1-\delta_k)\|x\|_2^2 \le \|Ax\|_2^2 \le (1+\delta_k)\|x\|_2^2$ for all $k$-sparse $x\in\R^n$. Smallest such $\delta_k$ is $\delta_k(A)$. Equivalently, $\delta_k(A)=\max_{|T|\le k}\|A_T^* A_T - I_{\R^T}\|$.

nodes.name: Sub-gaussian restricted isometries
nodes.statement: For sub-gaussian $m\times n$ matrix $A$ with independent rows or columns (per the two stated models): for every $1\le k\le n$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, if $m\ge C\delta^{-2} k\log(en/k)$ then $\delta_k(\bar A)\le\delta$ with prob $\ge 1-2\exp(-c\delta^2 m)$, where $\bar A = m^{-1/2} A$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.14
nodes.statement: Use equivalent form $\delta_k(A) = \max_{|T|=k}\|A_T^* A_T - I_{\R^T}\|$. For each $T$, the sub-matrix $A_T$ satisfies hypotheses of TP9.7 (rows model) or TP9.12 (columns model); apply LP9.11 then union bound over $\binom{n}{k}\le(en/k)^k$ choices of $T$.

nodes.name: Apply TP9.7 / TP9.12 to fixed $T$
nodes.statement: Fix $T\subseteq[n]$, $|T|=k$. Rows of $A_T$ are independent sub-gaussian isotropic in $\R^T$ (rows model) or columns of $A_T$ inherit sub-gaussian isotropic property (columns model). Then with prob $\ge 1-2\exp(-cs^2)$: $\sqrt m - C_0\sqrt k - s \le \smin(A_T) \le \smax(A_T) \le \sqrt m + C_0\sqrt k + s$.

nodes.name: Convert to RIP via LP9.11
nodes.statement: By LP9.11 applied to $\bar A_T$: $\|\bar A_T^* \bar A_T - I\| \le 3\max(\delta_0,\delta_0^2)$, $\delta_0 = C_0\sqrt{k/m} + s/\sqrt m$.

nodes.name: Union bound + choose $s$
nodes.statement: Union bound over $\binom n k \le (en/k)^k$ subsets $T$. Choose $s = C_1\sqrt{k\log(en/k)} + \e\sqrt m$, then $\e=\delta/6$: with prob $\ge 1-2\exp(-c\e^2 m)$, $\delta_k(\bar A) \le \delta$.

nodes.name: Concentration implies restricted isometry
nodes.statement: If for every fixed $k$-sparse $x$, $\P\{(1-\delta)\|x\|^2 \le \|Ax\|^2 \le (1+\delta)\|x\|^2\}\ge 1-\exp(-\e m)$, then if $m\ge C\e^{-1} k\log(en/k)$ we have $\delta_k(\bar A)\le 2\delta$ with prob $\ge 1-\exp(-\e m/2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of PrP9.4
nodes.statement: For each $T$ ($|T|=k$) take net $\NN_T$ of $S^{n-1}\cap\R^T$ with $|\NN_T|\le 9^k$ via LP9.1. By LP9.3, $\|A_T^* A_T - I\| \le 2\max_{x\in\NN_T}|\|Ax\|^2-1|$. Union bound over $\binom n k \cdot 9^k$ choices.

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed rows; uniform
nodes.statement: For $N\times d$ matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ ($1<N\le d$) with independent isotropic rows in $\R^d$ and $|a_{ij}|\le K$ a.s.: for every $1<n\le d$, $\E\max_{|T|\le n}\max_{j\le|T|} |s_j(A_T)-\sqrt N| \le Cl\sqrt n$, where $l=\log n\sqrt{\log d}\sqrt{\log N}$.

nodes.name: Uniform Rudelson's inequality
nodes.statement: For vectors $x_i\in\R^d$ ($1<N\le d$) with $\|x_i\|_\infty\le K$ and independent symmetric Bernoulli $\e_i$, every $1<n\le d$: $\E\max_{|T|\le n}\|\sum\e_i (x_i)_T\otimes(x_i)_T\| \le Cl\sqrt n\cdot\max_{|T|\le n}\|\sum (x_i)_T\otimes(x_i)_T\|^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Uniform deviation from 1
nodes.statement: For stochastic process $(Z_t)_{t\in\TT}$, $Z_t\ge 0$: $\E\sup_t|Z_t^2-1| \ge \max(\E\sup_t|Z_t-1|,(\E\sup_t|Z_t-1|)^2)$.

nodes.name: Symmetrization for stochastic processes
nodes.statement: For random vectors $X_{it}$ ($1\le i\le N$, $t\in\TT$ finite) such that $X_i=(X_{ti})_{t\in\TT}$ are independent in $B^\TT$, and i.i.d.\ Bernoulli $\e_i$: $\E\sup_t\|\sum(X_{it}-\E X_{it})\| \le 2\E\sup_t\|\sum\e_i X_{it}\|$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP9.17
nodes.statement: Apply LP9.12 with $X_i$ valued in product Banach space $B^\TT$ equipped with sup norm.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.15
nodes.statement: Three steps mirroring TP9.10: (1) symmetrize via LP9.17 to bring in Bernoulli signs; (2) apply uniform Rudelson PrP9.5 conditional on $A$, then Cauchy-Schwarz to get $E\le C_K l\sqrt{n/N}(E+1)^{1/2}$; (3) solve and diagonalize via LP9.16.

nodes.name: Uniform symmetrization
nodes.statement: $E := \E\max_{|T|\le n}\|N^{-1}A_T^* A_T - I\| \le (2/N)\E\max_{|T|\le n}\|\sum_i\e_i (A_i)_T\otimes(A_i)_T\|$ by LP9.17.

nodes.name: Apply uniform Rudelson + Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: Conditional on $A$, apply PrP9.5: $E \le (C_K l\sqrt n/\sqrt N) \E\max\|N^{-1} A_T^* A_T\|^{1/2}$. Triangle and Hölder give $E \le C_K l\sqrt{n/N}(E+1)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Solve and diagonalize
nodes.statement: Solving in $E$: $E\le\max(\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=C_K l\sqrt{2n/N}$. Diagonalization via uniform LP9.16 converts to bound on $\E\max_T\max_j|s_j(A_T)-\sqrt N|$.

nodes.name: Heavy-tailed restricted isometries
nodes.statement: For $m\times n$ matrix $A$ with independent isotropic rows in $\R^n$ and $|a_{ij}|\le K$ a.s., $m\le n$: for $1<k\le n$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, if $m\ge C\delta^{-2} k\log n\log^2 k\log(\delta^{-2} k\log n\log^2 k)$ then $\E\delta_k(\bar A)\le\delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP9.16
nodes.statement: Apply TP9.15 (equivalent form $E\le\max(\delta,\delta^2)$, $\delta=C_K l\sqrt{k/m}$); algebraic rearrangement of the resulting condition on $m$ yields the explicit bound.

nodes.name: Random Fourier measurements; sub-matrices of bounded orthogonal matrices
nodes.statement: Random row-submatrix of DFT or any bounded orthogonal $W$ (with $W^*W=nI$, $|w_{ij}|=O(1)$, e.g. Hadamard) satisfies hypotheses of TP9.16 with $K=1$, giving $m = O(k\log n\log^3 k)$ measurements suffice for sparse recovery.
